_readme: Keyed by theme key; each entry is an ordered list of { claim, direction, ids }. ids are full bloom-data.json record ids. direction is agree|disagree|divided|mixed, hand-assigned against each statement's actual polarity (it is not derivable from vote % alone). Themes with no entry here (access) render their page without a TOC or insights section. Note: datacenters' 'AI companies shouldn't get special treatment' cites p123, which under the current tag model belongs only to workforce (tags: Economic Benefit, Workforce & Labor). That is intentional: buildThemeView appends any insight-cited record missing from the theme's own statement list, so it still displays and pages correctly. Upstream applied a round of editorial decisions (references/Bloom-Theme-Insights-Statements w_ Decisions.xlsx) on top of the original verbatim insights: statements flagged as DIFFERENCEs rather than agreements were pulled from their insights, a few were moved between insights or added, one insight's claim was softened, and two insights (education's 'AI poses specific risks to learning and thinking' and agency's 'AI companies should prove they can prevent catastrophic outcomes') were removed entirely.

datacenters.claim: Data center development needs thorough environmental review and reporting
AI companies shouldn't get special treatment (though Optimists are less certain about the negative impacts)
The benefits of data centers are not well established
People disagree about whether data center benefits outweigh the costs

governance.claim: Communities should be involved in decisions about AI
Government use of AI should be transparent and independently audited
People disagree about whether AI should be publicly- or privately-owned
Some regulation of AI is necessary

education.claim: Schools need clear rules and transparency about AI use
Children need guardrails before AI is used with them
People disagree about how much AI erodes critical thinking and creativity
parents should be able to monitor their children's interactions with AI

mentalhealth.claim: People disagree about whether AI erodes social connection
AI chatbots are not an acceptable substitute for therapy

workforce.claim: Workers should know when AI is used to evaluate them
Companies that automate jobs should help fund retraining
The jobs AI replaces are essential
People disagree about AI companies' role in preparing the workforce

agency.claim: AI should strengthen human judgment, not replace it
People disagree about whether AI is fundamentally different from past technologies
People disagree about whether to adapt to AI or resist it
